# Data visualization {#sec-visualization}

Julia has three reasonable routes to graphics, all resting on
[**Makie.jl**](https://docs.makie.org) [@danisch2021makie]:

| Route | For whom |
|---|---|
| `TidierPlots.jl` | people coming from `ggplot2` who want the same grammar |
| `AlgebraOfGraphics.jl` | people who want an idiomatically Julian grammar of graphics |
| Plain `Makie.jl` | full control over the figure |

This chapter shows all three on the same data, because the right choice depends on the
task — and because knowing how to translate between them keeps you from getting stuck.

```{julia}
#| label: setup-06
using TidierData
using CairoMakie
using AlgebraOfGraphics
using CSV, DataFrames

CairoMakie.activate!(type = "png")

ponds = CSV.read(joinpath("..", "data", "ponds.csv"), DataFrame)
ponds_c = @chain ponds begin
    @drop_missing(canopy)
    @mutate(log_area = log(area_m2))
end

nrow(ponds_c)
```

## `TidierPlots.jl`: the ggplot grammar {#sec-tidierplots}

```{julia}
#| label: fig-tidierplots-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Richness against canopy cover, by region."
using TidierPlots

ggplot(ponds_c, @aes(x = canopy, y = richness, color = region)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(x = "Canopy cover (%)", y = "Species richness",
         title = "Richness declines with shading")
```

::: {.r-equivalent}
**In R**

```r
ggplot(ponds_c, aes(x = canopy, y = richness, colour = region)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Canopy cover (%)", y = "Species richness")
```

The translation is nearly character for character; the difference is the `@` in
`@aes`.
:::

## `AlgebraOfGraphics.jl`: an algebraic grammar {#sec-aog}

AoG treats plots as an algebra: `*` combines layers, `+` superimposes them.

```{julia}
#| label: fig-aog-scatter
#| fig-cap: "The same plot in AlgebraOfGraphics, with a linear fit per region."
plt = AlgebraOfGraphics.data(ponds_c) *
      mapping(:canopy => "Canopy cover (%)",
              :richness => "Species richness",
              color = :region => "Region") *
      (visual(Scatter, alpha = 0.6) + AlgebraOfGraphics.linear())

draw(plt; figure = (size = (700, 450),))
```

::: {.callout-note}
`AlgebraOfGraphics.data` and `AlgebraOfGraphics.linear` are qualified because the
names `data` and `linear` collide with other loaded packages. In a script using only
AoG, `data(...)` and `linear()` suffice.
:::

## Facets {#sec-facets}

```{julia}
#| label: fig-facets
#| fig-cap: "Richness–area relationship faceted by hydroperiod."
plt = AlgebraOfGraphics.data(ponds_c) *
      mapping(:log_area => "log(area)",
              :richness => "Richness",
              color = :region,
              layout = :hydro) *
      (visual(Scatter, alpha = 0.6) + AlgebraOfGraphics.linear())

draw(plt; figure = (size = (800, 400),))
```

## Distributions {#sec-distributions}

```{julia}
#| label: fig-boxplot
#| fig-cap: "Richness distribution by region and hydroperiod."
plt = AlgebraOfGraphics.data(ponds_c) *
      mapping(:region => "Region",
              :richness => "Richness",
              color = :hydro => "Hydroperiod",
              dodge = :hydro) *
      visual(BoxPlot)

draw(plt; figure = (size = (700, 420),))
```

## Plain `Makie.jl`: full control {#sec-makie}

When a figure needs a layout the grammar cannot express, drop down to Makie.

```{julia}
#| label: fig-makie-composite
#| fig-cap: "A composite figure assembled by hand with Makie."
fig = Figure(size = (860, 380))

ax1 = Axis(fig[1, 1], xlabel = "Canopy cover (%)", ylabel = "Richness",
           title = "(a) Canopy")
scatter!(ax1, ponds_c.canopy, ponds_c.richness, color = (:steelblue, 0.6))

ax2 = Axis(fig[1, 2], xlabel = "log(area)", ylabel = "Richness",
           title = "(b) Area")
scatter!(ax2, ponds_c.log_area, ponds_c.richness, color = (:darkorange, 0.6))

ax3 = Axis(fig[1, 3], xlabel = "Richness", ylabel = "Frequency",
           title = "(c) Distribution")
hist!(ax3, ponds_c.richness, bins = 12, color = (:seagreen, 0.7))

fig
```

Makie's layout system is grid-based (`fig[row, col]`), covering the role of
`patchwork` and `cowplot` in R without an extra package.

## Saving figures {#sec-saving}

```{julia}
#| label: saving
#| eval: false
save("figure.png", fig; px_per_unit = 3)   # high-resolution raster
save("figure.pdf", fig)                    # vector, for publication
save("figure.svg", fig)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Choosing a backend

`CairoMakie` produces publication-quality static output (PNG, PDF, SVG) and is what
this book uses. `GLMakie` opens GPU-accelerated interactive windows — useful for
exploring data, unsuitable for rendering a book.
:::

## Exercises {.unnumbered}

1. Redo @fig-tidierplots-scatter using `temp_c` on the x axis. Does the pattern hold?
2. Build a two-panel figure: richness by region on the left, focal-species occurrence
   proportion by region on the right.
3. Translate @fig-facets to `TidierPlots.jl` using `facet_wrap`.
